key_insight: A simplified room-temperature continuous-variable photonic QNN can classify oral-cancer smartphone images with fewer parameters than both a standard CV-QNN and a classical baseline, while matching or exceeding performance in the best setting.
engineering_relevance: This points to parameter-efficient quantum models as a plausible edge-AI option for medical image screening where cryogenic qubit hardware and large model footprints are impractical.
method: MobileNetV1 extracts image features, then PCA compresses them to 16 dimensions.
A hybrid classical-CV QNN uses displacement, interferometric, and Kerr gates on a photonic backend.
A simplified Φ∘D∘U1 layer reduces trainable parameters by about 40–45% versus the standard CV-QNN layer.
evidence_signal: Across experiments, the four-qumode simplified CV-QNN achieved the highest validation AUC and 100% calibrated test accuracy across all seeds, using only 18 parameters and 67% fewer than the 55-parameter classical baseline.
watch_item: The performance advantage is width-dependent and the gains rely on PCA plus restricted encoding, so hardware scaling and deployment robustness still need careful validation.
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Continuous-Variable Photonic Quantum Neural Networks for Edge Quantum AI: Demonstration in Oral Cancer Detection
